sources.title: Morph public model metadata
sources.evidence: Exact morph-v3-large entry names v3 Large Apply, describes complex code editing, and declares text input/output, 262144 input-context tokens and 131072 output tokens. Its created timestamp is shared across current entries, so is not treated as a launch date. Reopened for the October 27 parameter re-audit: the exact Large entry still contains neither a total/active parameter count nor a named base-model or Hugging Face lineage identifier.

sources.title: Morph complete API documentation: Apply API and Code Apply API
sources.evidence: Reopened and searched the complete documentation for exact Large mentions, nominal counts, base-model and fine-tuning statements on October 27. Apply tables distinguish morph-v3-large from morph-v3-fast and auto; Large is for complex changes. The Apply Model page repeats a generic 7B speed claim, while the CLI explicitly calls Large the larger model. No exact Large total/active count or named base-model lineage was found. The earlier capability assessment remains unchanged.

sources.title: Fast Apply: Code Merging at 10,500 tok/s for AI Agents
sources.evidence: Reopened March 5, 2026 guide for the October 27 re-audit. Its developer-published 7B nominal count accompanies 10500 tok/s and $0.80/M input, matching the Fast row. The separate Large row gives 5000+ tok/s and $0.90/M input without a parameter count. The architecture and FAQ repeat the generic 7B claim but do not explicitly map it to Large or identify a base checkpoint.

sources.title: Morph Models
sources.evidence: Separates hosted open-weight general coding models from specialized agent models, explicitly listing morph-v3-large as Fast Apply (large) for difficult edits.

sources.title: Morph End User License Agreement
sources.evidence: January 13, 2026 EULA covers Morph services and model weights where applicable, grants limited revocable use, and characterizes underlying Morph models and weights as proprietary technology. Open-source components are exceptions only when separately identified.

sources.title: Optimizing Models to Be Fast at Codegen
sources.evidence: Reopened June 19, 2026 first-party research. It describes trained speculators and optimized serving, including an under-30B small-model discussion, but gives no exact morph-v3-large count or named backbone. Its Qwen weights statement concerns hosted open-model serving and does not identify Large as a particular Qwen fine-tune. Neither those examples nor drafter sizes support an inherited Large count.

sources.title: Fast Apply Makes Faster Agents
sources.evidence: November 4, 2025 article search-index text describes attention/feed-forward kernels, pruned vocabulary and hierarchical positional encodings for Fast Apply generically; no exact Large specification is established. Direct page currently exposes title/date/table of contents without article body, so indexed text is treated as limited evidence.

sources.title: Morph Gets Faster: 10,500+ Tokens Per Second
sources.evidence: Dated June 15, 2025. Both web extraction and browser inspection expose title/date and table of contents but not article body. This access limitation prevents checking whether its model-selection section establishes earlier Large availability; it does not verify July 7.

sources.title: Morph V3 Large API Pricing and Providers
sources.evidence: Catalog lists July 7, 2025 as Released and identifies the code-apply model. This corroborates the catalog date but is not an original developer launch announcement and does not establish earliest public availability.

sources.title: Models.dev Morph V3 Large catalog entry
sources.evidence: Baseline lead was inspected. Its comment says lab metadata was carried over from the OpenRouter catalog; it asserts July 7 and false reasoning/tools without cited primary capability classification, and contains the unsupported generic flagship description.

sources.title: Apply Model - Morph Documentation
sources.evidence: Freshly inspected October 27. The overview attributes 10500-token/s code merging to a nominal 7B model. The adjacent table lists morph-v3-fast at 10500+ tok/sec and morph-v3-large at 2500+ tok/sec, and its example selects morph-v3-fast. No Large-specific total/active count or explicit named base-model lineage is given.

sources.title: morph CLI - Morph Documentation
sources.evidence: Freshly fetched directly with HTTP 200 and cross-checked against llms-full.txt on October 27 after the web extractor could not open this URL. The Apply an edit section calls morph-v3-large the larger model. This supports treating it as a distinct size option, but supplies no numeric count, dense/MoE classification or named base checkpoint.

sources.title: Morph V3 Fast and Large introduction, June 15, 2025
sources.evidence: Reopened October 27 in the live browser: after rendering, the complete body explicitly introduces Morph v3 as a step up from the previous model, names morph-v3-fast at 10,500+ tok/s and morph-v3-large at 5,000+ tok/s, and offers API access. The article is dated June 15, 2025 and authored by Tejas Bhakta. This exact-generation introduction was missing from the previous static extraction, which returned only the title/date/table of contents.

parameters_b.note: Fresh October 27 search did not establish a nominal total for morph-v3-large or explicit fine-tune/post-training lineage to a named base model. Morph publishes 7B for generic Fast Apply beside the 10500 tok/s and $0.80/M offering, while its tables separate Large and its CLI calls Large the larger model. The unresolved issue is exact-variant attribution, not a missing tensor census; neither the sibling 7B claim nor an illustrative Qwen/drafter size is transferred.

active_parameters_b.note: Rechecked separately on October 27: no active-parameter count or active counting convention for morph-v3-large appears in the exact metadata, complete docs, Apply Model page or later inference research. No exact Large dense/MoE classification or named-base lineage was established, so active parameters are not inferred from the generic 7B total or from serving speed.

architecture.note: Generic Fast Apply discussion mentions specialized merging architecture and serving kernels, but does not establish the exact Large backbone or dense/MoE classification. FP8 and speculative decoding are serving properties, not sufficient architecture evidence.

context_window.note: Exact first-party model metadata specifies max_context_length 262144 tokens. Some integration/provider limits differ; retain the explicit direct model metadata value.

modalities.note: Exact metadata explicitly declares text input and output; API merges source-code text.

reasoning.note: Fast Apply is classified as specialized merging with planning performed upstream, but no exact-variant explicit negative reasoning-mode classification was verified. Missing reasoning keys do not prove false; clear the baseline boolean.

tool_call.note: The model is invoked inside another agent edit tool and returns code, but that is not an explicit declaration that the model cannot issue structured tool calls. No exact primary negative classification was verified; clear false rather than infer it from absent metadata.

sources.label: Morph V3 Fast and Large introduction

patch.notes: V3 Large is a specialized code-apply model, distinct from V3 Fast and Morph-hosted general coding models. The October 27 parameter re-audit reopened exact metadata, full documentation, the Fast Apply guide and later inference research, and searched for nominal counts and explicit base-model lineage. The generic developer 7B claim accompanies the Fast-speed/pricing offering; the CLI explicitly calls V3 Large the larger model. No nominal Large total or named base checkpoint was established, so total remains unverified and active count undisclosed. This is an attribution limitation, not a requirement for an exact tensor census. Backbone remains unverified. The fully rendered developer introduction establishes June 15, 2025 for V3 Fast and Large; July 7 is a later provider-catalog date. Reasoning/tool-call support remains unverified because absent metadata is not a negative classification. Current documented specifications were checked; endpoint operation was not tested.

summary: October 27 parameter re-audit leaves total parameters unverified and active parameters undisclosed after fresh primary-source and lineage searches. Newly checked Apply Model and CLI documentation distinguish the generic 7B Fast offering from V3 Large, explicitly described as the larger model, without giving Large a numeric size or named base. Preserves the earlier specialized-code-editing description, proprietary licensing, verified context/modalities and unresolved capability assessments. The October 27 release-date re-audit recovers the complete rendered developer V3 introduction and verifies June 15, 2025, preserving all thirteen other field assessments.

findings: The previous failure was incomplete client-rendered article extraction, not absence of exact developer launch evidence.
The new-v3 wording names both exact variants and offers immediate API use.
The generic changelog and mutable created metadata were not substituted for the exact article.
limitations: The article is current publisher content, not an archived historical snapshot; no authenticated inference was performed.
